chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated from Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Mu'adhi, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us from Musa ibn Isma'il, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both).

He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) had a friend who was carefree/frivolous, and he delayed visiting him for several days. One day he came to him, and Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: 'How did you spend the morning?' He said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I spent the morning contrary to what I love, and what Allah loves, and what the Satan loves!' Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) laughed and then said: 'How is that?' He said: 'Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves that I obey Him and do not disobey Him, but I am not like that; and the Satan loves that I disobey Allah and do not obey Him, but I am not like that; and I love that I do not die, but I am not like that.'

Then a man stood up to him and said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, why is it that we dislike death and do not love it?' He said: Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Because you have ruined your Hereafter and built up your worldly life, and you dislike the transition from habitation (prosperity) to ruin (destruction).'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, the present world

ai.seo_question: Why do humans naturally dislike death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the psychological root of death anxiety as the dissonance between worldly attachment (*al-'imarah*) and spiritual neglect. It underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing temporal life with eternal preparation, warning that excessive investment in the transient world leads to fear of the inevitable transition to the Hereafter.

en.basel-kadem: 28.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Hammad bin Isa, from Abdullah bin Qasem, from Abdullah bin Sinan, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:
There is no right hand (valid in promise) in the case of anger, nor in coercion, nor in compulsion.

He said: I said: May Allah rectify you, then what is the difference between compulsion and coercion? He said: Coercion is from the ruler, and compulsion is from a wife and a father, and that is nothing.
